overview: SEEK operates market-leading online employment marketplaces in Australia, New Zealand and six Asian markets (Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand), matching candidates and hirers through a two-sided platform monetised primarily via tiered, variable-priced job advertisements. Beyond its core APAC marketplaces, SEEK owns the Sidekicker contingent-labour marketplace and JobAdder applicant-tracking software, and holds non-controlled minority stakes in Zhaopin (China, 23.5%), BDjobs (Bangladesh) and Worxphere/JobKorea (South Korea), plus an 83.8% economic interest in the independently managed SEEK Growth Fund (HR SaaS, online education and contingent labour investments). SEEK is ASX-listed and headquartered in Melbourne; FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) continuing-operations net revenue was A$1,199m, split roughly 79% ANZ / 21% Asia.

business_model.summary: SEEK charges hirers to post job advertisements on a bespoke variable-pricing model (tiered Lite/Basic/Advanced/Premium ads) that scales price with the value of the likely placement; candidates use the marketplace for free. Growth is driven by a 'yield' strategy (price/value per ad) layered on top of largely flat-to-declining ad volumes, supplemented by adjacent sourcing, workflow and labour-hire products (Talent Search, SEEK Pass, Employer Brand Boost, JobAdder, Sidekicker).

revenue_streams.name: Expanded sourcing solutions (JobAdder, Sidekicker, Talent Search, SEEK Pass)

business_model.customer_type: B2B (hirers/employers of all sizes pay for ads and services) with a free B2C candidate side; marketplace model with network effects between the two
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia/New Zealand ~79% of net revenue, Asia (HK, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand) ~21%; minority equity-accounted exposure to China (Zhaopin), Bangladesh (BDjobs) and South Korea (Worxphere) sits outside segment revenue

main_competitors: Local/regional Asian job boards and classifieds
competitive_position.market_position: Clear market leader in Australia (35.5% placement share, 91% unaided brand awareness) and across its Asia footprint (25.4% placement share, 59% unaided awareness); LinkedIn estimated to account for under 10% of Australian placements

moat_factors.description: Two-sided marketplace with 60m+ candidate profiles and 360,000+ hirer relationships; scale on each side attracts the other, reinforcing matching quality
750m+ data points captured daily (searches, applications, availability, verified credentials, hirer shortlists) that cannot be replicated by AI-native entrants lacking historical placement outcomes
Nearly 30 years of brand building, verification (16m+ verified candidate credentials) and trust & safety infrastructure against scams/fraud
JobAdder ATS integration and embedded hiring workflows increase stickiness with recruiters and larger hirers
Single APAC product/tech platform (completed 2024) enables faster, cheaper product rollout than fragmented regional competitors

weaknesses: Revenue growth increasingly reliant on price/yield increases rather than volume, raising questions about the ceiling on hirer willingness to pay
Core job-ad volumes declining in both ANZ and Asia amid soft macro conditions and freemium transition in Asia
Reported earnings distorted and weakened by legacy non-core holdings (Zhaopin, SEEK Growth Fund) outside management's direct control
Perceived vulnerability to AI-native, direct candidate-to-employer matching tools that could bypass centralised job boards
Asia business still sub-scale relative to ANZ and more exposed to weaker regional macro (e.g., Hong Kong)

growth_drivers: Yield growth via deeper product adoption (Advanced/Premium ad tiers, AI candidate targeting) and value-based pricing linked to hirer ROI - 18% APAC yield growth in FY2026, sixth consecutive year of double-digit growth
AI-enabled product rollout (matching, targeting, verification) leveraging unique proprietary data and trust advantages that management argues compound rather than erode with AI adoption
Completed APAC platform unification (2024) enabling faster, cheaper, more reliable product deployment and supporting operating leverage (four consecutive halves of positive operating leverage)
Freemium rollout now complete across Asia, expanding total ad/hirer base even as paid volumes soften, building a funnel for future monetisation
Expansion into adjacent recruitment-value-chain products: reacquisition of Sidekicker (contingent labour, May 2025) and integration of JobAdder (ATS)

Potential capital unlock from SEEK Growth Fund's next phase (stated intention to sell its Employment Hero stake; broader asset sales under discussion) improving liquidity and simplifying the earnings picture
Structural, multi-year digitisation/penetration runway for online recruitment in several Asian markets

business.description: SEEK's own 'Principal Risks' disclosure flags that AI reshaping candidate/hirer discovery and behaviour could reduce activity, market share and revenue if SEEK fails to adapt; this is the dominant market narrative behind the 2026 share-price de-rating
Australia ad volumes -2% and Asia paid ad volumes -12% in FY2026; growth currently depends on yield/price increases offsetting volume softness
Scams, fraudulent verification and scrutiny of algorithmic pricing could erode candidate/hirer trust and revenue

financial.description: Net debt of A$962.4m at 30 June 2026 (borrowings A$1,093m) with net interest expense of A$66.4m in FY2026

financial.risk: Non-cash impairments and fair-value swings on legacy holdings
financial.description: A$356m total Zhaopin-related impairment and a 13% fall in the SEEK Growth Fund's portfolio value drove a A$306.5m statutory loss from continuing operations in FY2026 despite underlying operating growth

~21% of net revenue and sizeable intangible asset balances are denominated in Asian currencies (HKD, MYR, SGD, IDR, PHP, THB); AUD strength was a headwind to FY2026 translated results and goodwill carrying values

regulatory.risk: Sovereign and regulatory risk across eight countries of operation
regulatory.description: Changes in employment, data-privacy or other regulation in any ANZ or Asia market could adversely affect operations
Expanding use of AI in matching/candidate assessment could face new compliance obligations, hallucination/bias risk and legal liability
Operating across multiple jurisdictions with large pools of candidate/hirer data increases privacy-breach exposure

macro.description: A prolonged downturn in hiring activity in any major market (especially Australia) would directly reduce job ad volumes and revenue; FY2026 already showed softening Australian and Hong Kong conditions
Moderate net debt load means financing costs are sensitive to AUD and USD rate movements, though the business itself is not capital intensive

execution.description: Heavy reliance on SaaS, cloud and AI vendors increases exposure to a major incident that could disrupt services or breach data
Sidekicker (reacquired May 2025) required remediation of cybersecurity, workplace health & safety and payroll compliance gaps; JobAdder integration ongoing
SEEK does not control the Fund; the timing, pricing and structure of any future asset sales or liquidity mechanism rest with the Fund's Trustee and Manager, not SEEK
Employee survey data shows job-security concerns linked to AI and cost discipline, even as overall engagement scores rose

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Online employment marketplaces remain structurally advantaged over print/offline recruitment, with further digitisation runway in several Asian markets; ANZ is mature but SEEK continues to grow through pricing/yield and product depth rather than volume
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - job ad volumes track employment/hiring activity and have softened in FY2026 amid weaker Australian and Hong Kong macro conditions; revenue is more resilient than volumes because of SEEK's pricing power
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - ~A$1.1bn of borrowings and cross-currency interest rate swaps mean financing costs move with AUD/USD rates, but the underlying marketplace business has low capital intensity
key_input_costs: Cloud/IT infrastructure and AI compute costs
Management fees paid to the SEEK Growth Fund's external Manager

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: continuing-operations sales revenue up 17% to A$1,284.2m, net revenue up 10% to A$1,198.9m, EBITDA up 15% to A$529.9m, adjusted profit up 28% to A$199.1m, but a A$356m total impairment related to Zhaopin plus a 13% fall in the SEEK Growth Fund's valuation drove a statutory loss attributable to SEEK of A$306.5m (vs a A$238.3m profit in FY2025); record full-year dividend of 52 cents fully franked (up 13%)

Shares fell roughly 9-14% on the results day as FY2027 guidance implied decelerating growth and reinforced market concerns about long-term AI disruption to the job-board model, despite operating metrics being broadly in line with or ahead of budget

FY2027 guidance issued (first time): revenue of ~A$1,210-1,280m, EBITDA of ~A$530-580m, adjusted profit of ~A$185-215m, total expenditure of ~A$825-860m and capex of ~A$145-160m, implying mid-single-digit revenue growth with cost growth capped near 5%

UBS flagged that the FY2027 adjusted NPAT guidance midpoint came in ~7% below its prior estimate, citing weaker Asian volumes, currency effects and higher depreciation, while still raising its price target modestly to A$19.70

SEEK shares fell roughly 34-50% over the year as investors re-rated job boards on AI-disruption fears, in contrast with Indeed's parent Recruit Holdings, whose shares rose about 25% over the same period
Greg Roebuck became Chairman (having joined the Board as an independent non-executive director in December 2025), succeeding Graham Goldsmith after seven years as Chairman

H1 FY2026 result: double-digit net revenue and EBITDA growth (EBITDA +19%), record interim dividend of 27 cents, initially well received before the broader AI-disruption narrative took hold later in the year
SEEK reacquired 100% of Sidekicker (contingent labour marketplace) from the SEEK Growth Fund, subsequently remediating cybersecurity, WHS and payroll-compliance gaps identified post-acquisition

SEEK Growth Fund's total portfolio value fell 13% year-on-year; the Fund announced an intention to sell its stake in Employment Hero and is in advanced discussions with SEEK on the Fund's 'next phase' and liquidity mechanisms, including potential sale of assets valued at over A$1bn

Zhaopin: continued discussions on simplifying its ownership structure contributed to a A$283.6m write-down of the equity-accounted investment and a A$72.4m impairment of the receivable from the 2021 Zhaopin sell-down

items.metric: Revenue (continuing operations, excl. Fund and significant items)
items.notes: Midpoint implies ~5% revenue growth in constant currency vs FY2026's A$1,284.2m sales revenue / A$1,198.9m net revenue base
Midpoint implies ~6% growth in constant currency vs FY2026 EBITDA of A$529.9m
Midpoint of ~A$200m implies roughly flat-to-modest growth vs FY2026 adjusted profit of A$199.1m; UBS estimated the midpoint ran ~7% below its prior forecast
Implies cost growth capped at roughly 5%, continuing the operating-leverage discipline of FY2026 (revenue +10% vs cost +8%)
Compares with A$151.7m actual capex in FY2026, continued investment in product/technology and AI capability

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Ian Narev stated FY2026 results for revenue, EBITDA, adjusted NPAT and costs were all within FY2026 budget and guidance ranges, and that productivity savings have been built into the FY2027 budget with further commitments identified for FY2028 and beyond. Management reiterated confidence that SEEK's combination of proprietary data, trust and existing hirer/candidate relationships lets it leverage AI better than competitors, while acknowledging that 'the broader environment of uncertainty regarding the impact of AI on technology companies has made it harder to translate our belief into market confidence.'

bull_case: Durable #1 marketplace position across ANZ and most Asian markets, with strong network effects (60m+ candidate profiles, 360,000+ hirer relationships) and brand (91% unaided awareness in Australia) that are hard for new entrants to replicate

Management argues - and FY2026 yield data (18% APAC growth, sixth straight year of double-digit growth) supports - that SEEK's proprietary, decades-deep placement data and trust infrastructure let it harness AI as a moat-widener rather than a disruptor

Share price has de-rated sharply (down roughly a third to a half over the past year) even as underlying EBITDA, adjusted profit and dividends kept growing double digits, creating a valuation gap versus broker price targets clustered around A$18-20+

Completed platform unification and ongoing AI-enabled product rollout are delivering genuine operating leverage (four consecutive halves of cost growth below revenue growth) and record dividends (52cps FY2026, up 13%)

Optionality to simplify/monetise non-core holdings - SEEK Growth Fund's stated intent to sell its Employment Hero stake and ongoing discussions on the Fund's next phase, alongside the Zhaopin stake - could remove earnings volatility and unlock capital over time
bear_case: The core investment debate is whether AI-native tools will let candidates and hirers match directly, bypassing centralised job boards altogether; this fear, not SEEK's current fundamentals, is what drove the 2026 share-price collapse

Underlying job ad volumes are already declining (Australia -2%, Asia paid ads -12% in FY2026), with growth increasingly dependent on price/yield increases whose ceiling is untested and could trigger hirer pushback or trading down to free/lower tiers

FY2027 guidance signals deceleration (mid-single-digit revenue growth, adjusted profit roughly flat at the midpoint) and came in below some analysts' prior expectations, reinforcing the market's loss of confidence rather than resolving it

Reported earnings are repeatedly distorted by large, largely uncontrollable non-cash items from legacy non-core holdings - A$356m of Zhaopin impairments and a 13% Growth Fund valuation decline drove a A$306.5m statutory loss in FY2026 - complicating the investment case and governance oversight

Meaningful exposure to Asian currency translation and a softer Asia macro backdrop (notably Hong Kong) adds volatility on top of the AI-disruption overhang, while net debt of ~A$962m leaves some sensitivity to interest rates
